description: One load of fruit, weighed onto somebody else's scale. The packer keeps the original; this is the grower's copy, and it is the only weight the grower controls. Gross minus tare is net, computed here rather than taken, because the arithmetic on a thermal slip is the first thing a settlement disagreement is about. A ticket is Draft while the phone still has it, Submitted once it is filed, and Matched once a Settlement Statement claims it — which is the whole point of keeping tickets: a settlement that pays for less fruit than was delivered can only be seen by somebody holding both halves.

fields.description: The number printed on the packer's own ticket. Not this record's docname — the two are different registers, and a settlement dispute is argued in the packer's numbering.
fields.label: Ticket Number

fields.description: The day the load crossed the scale.
fields.label: Date

fields.description: The packer or shipper the fruit was delivered to, as a Customer.
fields.label: Customer

fields.description: Free text on purpose. A packer writes what a packer writes, and forcing it onto an Item list at capture time is how a ticket goes unrecorded.
fields.label: Variety

fields.description: Computed, never typed. Draft is a ticket still on the phone; Submitted is one that has been filed; Matched is one a Settlement Statement has claimed; Cancelled is a submitted ticket withdrawn.
fields.label: Status

fields.description: The Settlement Statement that paid for this load, once one does. Set by matching, not by hand.
fields.label: Settlement

fields.description: Truck and fruit together, as the scale read it.
fields.label: Gross Weight

fields.description: The empty truck, and the bins if the packer tares them.
fields.label: Tare Weight

fields.description: Gross minus tare. COMPUTED, never taken as input — a net weight somebody typed is a number with no arithmetic behind it, and this is the figure a settlement is checked against.
fields.label: Net Weight

fields.description: The unit all three weights are in. One unit per ticket: a gross in pounds and a tare in kilos is a net of nothing.
fields.label: Weight UOM
Where It Came From, Where It Went

fields.description: The Field the load was picked from, where the operation tracks fields.
fields.label: Field

fields.description: The block within the field, as the crew calls it.
fields.label: Block

fields.description: The packing house, cold storage or yard the load was taken to.
fields.label: Destination

fields.description: The photograph of the paper ticket. Keep it: a thermal slip in a truck door pocket is unreadable by the time a settlement arrives, and this is the only thing that outlives a disagreement about what the scale said.
fields.label: Ticket Image
